title: Norms give invertible sheaves and sections with saturated nonvanishing loci
statement:
Let $p:Y	o Z$ be a finite surjective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Fix an integer $d\geq1$ and maps $
u_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ for all open $V\subseteq Z$, compatible with restriction and preserving multiplication and $1$. Suppose $
u_V(p^\sharp a)=a^d$ for every $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, and that $b(y)=0$ implies $
u_V(b)(p(y))=0$ for every $b\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $y\in p^{-1}V$, where values are in residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. For every invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] there is an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $N$ such that for every $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ there is $t\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$ satisfying $$Z_t=Z\setminus p(Y\setminus Y_s)=\{z\in Z:\ p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s\}.$$ The tensor powers and nonvanishing opens $Y_s,Z_t$ have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; no ampleness of $M$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BCY (divisors-lemma-norm-invertible) and 0BCZ (divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible), applied to sections of tensor powers; Section 0BCX (divisors-section-norms) specifies the norm hypotheses.

proof.text: For each $z\in Z$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs] to the finite morphism $p$ and the invertible module $M$. Choose the resulting neighborhood $V_z$ and a trivialization $\mathcal O_Y|_{p^{-1}V_z}\cong M|_{p^{-1}V_z}$. The image $e_z$ of $1$ is a generating section: multiplication by $e_z$ is this trivialization. Since $z\in V_z$, these opens cover $Z$. Fix this cover and these frames before choosing $n$ or $s$.

Apply [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing] to this fixed cover, its generators, and the given restriction-compatible multiplicative maps $
u$. Obtain a single invertible module $N$ with generators $f_i$ and transitions $
u(u_{ij})$. Fix any $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$. The lemma says that $e_i^{\otimes n}$ generates, so there is a unique regular function $b_i$ on $p^{-1}V_i$ with $s|_{p^{-1}V_i}=b_i e_i^{\otimes n}$. Its section clause supplies $t$ with $t|_{V_i}=
u_{V_i}(b_i)f_i^{\otimes n}$. The module $N$ was fixed before $n$ and $s$.

Fix $n,s,t$ as above and any $z\in Z$; choose $i$ with $z\in V_i$ from the cover. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-function-norm-nonvanishing] to $p$, the given family $
u$, and $b_i\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V_i,\mathcal O_Y)$: $p$ is finite and the unitality, multiplicativity, restriction and residue-field vanishing assumptions are exactly those of the item. It gives $
u_{V_i}(b_i)(z)
e0$ if and only if $b_i(y)
e0$ for every $y$ above $z$. By [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing], the frames of both tensor powers are generators. Their values are bases of the one-dimensional residue-field fibres; multiplying such a basis by a scalar is zero exactly when that scalar is zero. The local formulas for $s,t$ therefore identify the two sides with $z\in Z_t$ and $p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s$, using [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for these loci. Thus $Z_t=\{z:p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s\}$.

For any set map $p$, the condition $p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s$ means that no point of $Y\setminus Y_s$ maps to $z$. It is therefore equivalent to $z\in Z\setminus p(Y\setminus Y_s)$, proving both required equalities.

lean.statement: theorem exists_invertible_norm_sections {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ Z) [IsFinite p] [Surjective p] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (ν : ∀ V : Z.Opens, Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ V) →* Γ(Z, V)) (hν_restrict : ∀ (V W : Z.Opens) (h : W ≤ V) (b : Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ V)), ν W (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (p.preimage_mono h)).op b) = Z.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op (ν V b)) (hν_power : ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (a : Γ(Z, V)), ν V (p.app V a) = a ^ d) (hν_vanish : ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (b : Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ V)) (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ p ⁻¹ᵁ V), Y.evaluation (p ⁻¹ᵁ V) y hy b = 0 → Z.evaluation V (p y) hy (ν V b) = 0) (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : ∃ N : Z.Modules, N.IsInvertible ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (s : Γ(M.tensorPow n, ⊤)), ∃ t : Γ(N.tensorPow n, ⊤), nonvanishingLocus (N.tensorPow n) t = (p '' (nonvanishingLocus (M.tensorPow n) s)ᶜ)ᶜ ∧ nonvanishingLocus (N.tensorPow n) t = {z : Z | p ⁻¹' {z} ⊆ nonvanishingLocus (M.tensorPow n) s}
